{"obligations":{"reduction":{"status":"written_and_valid","quote":null,"witness":null,"load_bearing":null},"lower_bound":{"status":"not_written","quote":"The pair \((a,b)\) and the pair \(\bigl(\min(a,b),|a-b|\bigr)\) have the
same gcd:
\[
\gcd(a,b)=\gcd\bigl(\min(a,b),|a-b|\bigr)
\tag{3}
\]
(standard; details omitted).","witness":"The missing all-cases statement is: for every nonnegative a,b, gcd(a,b) divides both min(a,b) and |a-b|, so it divides the new pair's gcd. The passage merely asserts the identity and explicitly omits its proof.","load_bearing":"This is the direction preventing the primewise gcd invariant from decreasing during a move. Without it, the claimed invariant—and hence the forced terminal exponents—has not been established."},"upper_bound":{"status":"not_written","quote":"The pair \((a,b)\) and the pair \(\bigl(\min(a,b),|a-b|\bigr)\) have the
same gcd:
\[
\gcd(a,b)=\gcd\bigl(\min(a,b),|a-b|\bigr)
\tag{3}
\]
(standard; details omitted).","witness":"The missing all-cases statement is: every common divisor of min(a,b) and |a-b| divides both a and b; this requires considering which of a,b is the minimum and reconstructing the maximum as min(a,b)+|a-b|. No such argument is written.","load_bearing":"This reverse divisibility prevents the primewise gcd invariant from increasing. It is necessary for the equality used to recover each exponent of M from the initial board."}},"S_valid":0,"wrong_answer_stated":false,"notes":"Mapping: lower_bound is forward common-divisor preservation; upper_bound is reverse reconstruction.
